paper.title_en: Lattice QCD Calculations of Transverse-Momentum-Dependent Distributions
paper.abstract_en: Transverse-Momentum-Dependent Distributions (TMDs) provide a unique window into the three-dimensional structure of hadrons, encoding correlations between parton transverse motion and spin that are inaccessible to collinear parton distribution functions (PDFs). Lattice QCD (LQCD) offers a first-principles framework for computing TMDs, overcoming the limitations of phenomenological extractions from experimental data. This talk reviews recent progress in lattice QCD calculations of TMDs, focusing on the role of Large Momentum Effective Theory (LaMET) in connecting Euclidean lattice observables to physical lightcone TMDs. I discuss key developments in the determination of the Collins-Soper (CS) kernel, intrinsic soft functions, TMD parton distribution functions (TMDPDFs), and TMD wave functions (TMDWFs), as well as novel approaches such as the Coulomb gauge (CG) method. I also highlight ongoing challenges and future directions for lattice TMD physics, including precision determinations, gluon TMD calculations, and synergy with experimental programs and beyond.
